limits: Fresh process is not a cold operating-system cache. Untimed validation or warmup processes may warm file or library caches; each timed subject is nevertheless launched anew.

Input-file opening, source or AOT preparation, pin hashing and output validation occur outside the measured process interval. Runtime startup, loading, in-process JIT or interpretation, required workload, output production and shutdown occur inside it.
Lightweight watchdog, process-registration or resource-monitor operations differ by harness and can overlap the timed interval. No overhead subtraction was found.

Historical producer sealing is incomplete. In particular the 95 selected retime profiles, 90 fast-scripting primary/policy profiles, 37 additional-language profiles and 18 primary array profiles have retained process-timing producer source, but those reports do not themselves seal the timing runner and imported compact helper. This review does not upgrade their historical integrity to a fully closed runtime or producer chain.

The exact run_remaining.py members are pinned for the 40 regexredux/pidigits/confirmation profiles. That proves the retained caller timer; it does not independently seal every imported dependency of those older runs.

The shared compact environment starts from os.environ and applies explicit worker/runtime overrides. Historical ambient variables are not comprehensively captured by older reports; absence of an unrecorded preload or runtime option cannot be inferred.

This is a timing-boundary and sample-attribution review, not a new validation of all sources, runtime closures, work obligations, compiler flags, thread ceilings or host conditions. Historical cross-date measurements are not one simultaneous matched cohort.

Several Clojure, Nim, Gleam and V-tree reports were inspected at retained original qualification paths because the public archive path map has no matching alias. Their locations and digests are recorded per report.
